readme.text:
# 📜 NFSFU234FormValidation

[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/nfsfu234-form-validation?style=for-the-badge)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/nfsfu234-form-validation)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/nfsfu234-form-validation?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/NFSFU234FormValidation/nfsfu234-form-validation/blob/main/LICENSE)
[![jsDelivr](https://data.jsdelivr.com/v1/package/npm/nfsfu234-form-validation/badge)](https://www.jsdelivr.com/package/npm/nfsfu234-form-validation)

A lightweight, dependency-free client-side form validation library for HTML forms - inputs, textareas, selects, radios, checkboxes, and file/image uploads - with inline or modal error messages, AJAX submission, and a declarative config layer for validating forms across a whole multi-page site.

Works in plain HTML/CSS/JS, and in React/Next.js projects (initialize it client-side, e.g. inside
Or via CDN, no build step required:

```html
<form id="loginForm">
  <input type="email" name="email" required>
  <input type="password" name="password" required>
  <button type="submit">Log in</button>
</form>
```
Validation rules are picked up automatically from standard HTML attributes (

, etc.) - no extra markup needed for the common cases.

## Validating a whole multi-page site at once

If you have many forms across many pages, register them all once (e.g. in a shared script included on every page) instead of hand-wiring each page:

A field's config rule overrides its HTML attributes where it sets a value; where the config is silent, the field's own attributes still apply.

## API reference

### Constructor

```ts
new NFSFU234FormValidation(formDetails?: { form?: string | HTMLElement, customErrorMessages?: object }, ajaxOptions?: object)
```

## What this library does *not* do

- No server-side validation, no email delivery, no database checks - it's entirely client-side.

's AJAX support sends validated data to whatever backend you already have; it doesn't provide one.
- Client-side password hashing is a convenience utility, not a security feature - hashing happens in the browser, so it doesn't protect a password in transit the way server-side hashing over TLS does.
